source.title: Late Holocene occupation history of the southernmost Adélie penguin colonies at Cape Royds and Cape Barne, Ross Island, Antarctica
source.author: Steven D. Emslie
source.source_type: published synthesis of archaeological field surveys plus older breeding records

units.historical_Cape_Barne: named coastal breeding area, NOT a particular 3-10m nest patch
units.Cape_Royds: nearby source colony with population-trend summaries
units.time: dated named survey or source-stated period, NOT a balanced annual panel

frozen_evidence_before_any_model.certainty: historic nesting debris mapped; no contemporaneous reproduction census
new nests and adults near Cape Barne reported across 1960s visits; exact number/year and egg fate unverified
five occupied breeding adult nests documented by Taylor and Wilson 1990, repeated by Emslie 2026
Emslie states abandonment after reoccupation; small numbers of pairs may have appeared in late 1990s; do not assert exact first vacancy year
one January site-sampling visit; do not label a full 2001/02 breeding season as rigorously censused absent
distinct intact pebble nests and guano observed Dec 2024; author reports site still abandoned, no quantitative modern breeding-pair census in paper

competing_causal_predictions.legacy_sufficient_alone: old intact pebble/guano patch by itself predicts reliable re-occupation regardless of colonist source and access; Cape Barne is a descriptive negative example under its original context, not a direct controlled falsification
competing_causal_predictions.legacy_times_colonist_supply: old nest legacy could enhance selection only at high supply of dispersers or at viable source colony growth; same-site reoccupancy state should vary with independently counted prospective first breeders after adjusting access
competing_causal_predictions.legacy_times_functional_access: same physical legacy could matter only when McMurdo Sound ice breakup permits timely water access and chicks' foraging; condition must be independently measured during breeding stage, not an annual ice mean
competing_causal_predictions.static_habitat_only: rock, slope, guano and access explain reoccupation independent of a site's previous nesting history after pre-existing habitat comparison
competing_causal_predictions.success_public_information: recently successful rather than merely old or failed nesting spots attract first breeders

necessary_outcomes_for_positive_causal_c: dated confirmed prior egg failure vs confirmed chick production vs original surveyed-never-used patch risk set
pre-arrival habitat access, social source supply and physical cue measurements
repeat independent sites of comparable landscape and reproductive season
identifiable new breeders distinct from returning prior banded incumbents
future breeding success with effort/detection controls
independent variation or ethical authorized intervention for physical-legacy causal contrast
prohibited: Do not transform Emslie 2026 narrative into a continuous 1912–2024 annual site-by-year time series
Do not treat a reported abandoned site as every single season surveyed absent
Do not call 2024 pebbles proof that each nest was left by 1988/89 breeders
Do not treat egg/nest observation in 1988 as confirmed fledged chicks
Do not interpret low Cape Royds abundance plus Barne abandonment as a measured emigration causal effect
Do not infer a 2026 newly discovered physical engineering mechanism or publish 2026 cited historical events as original field data
Do not use antiquity of pebble soils as proof physical nesting-site quality stayed suitable at all dates
Do not amend frozen Ecology PR189, locked PR142 or separate emperor PR195
